items.explanation: The Marshall Plan, formally the European Recovery Program announced by Secretary of State George Marshall at Harvard on June 5, 1947, became the initiative the speech launched. Choice A is wrong because the Eisenhower Doctrine came a decade later (1957) and addressed the Middle East, not European recovery. Choice B is wrong because NATO was a military alliance signed in 1949, not the economic-aid program Marshall announced. Marshall Plan aid totaled $13.3 billion to sixteen Western European nations between 1948 and 1952, anchoring containment through economic stabilization.
items.explanationEs: El Plan Marshall, formalmente el Programa de Recuperación Europea anunciado por el Secretario de Estado George Marshall en Harvard el 5 de junio de 1947, fue la iniciativa que lanzó el discurso. La opción A es incorrecta porque la Doctrina Eisenhower llegó una década después (1957) y abordó el Medio Oriente, no la recuperación europea. La opción B es incorrecta porque la OTAN fue una alianza militar firmada en 1949, no el programa de ayuda económica que anunció Marshall. La ayuda del Plan Marshall sumó 13.300 millones de dólares para dieciséis naciones de Europa Occidental entre 1948 y 1952, sosteniendo la contención mediante la estabilización económica.

choices.text: Personal conflicts between Roosevelt, Churchill, and Stalin made sustained military cooperation nearly impossible.
choices.explanation: The source points to ideology, not personalities. The three leaders in fact sustained working cooperation through the war.
choices.misconception: substitutes personal friction for the structural cause the source names

choices.explanation: The Allies did not share all military technology — the United States withheld the atomic programme from the Soviets entirely.
choices.misconception: assumes full technology sharing among the Allies

choices.text: The creation of the United Nations divided the Allies into competing blocs before the war even ended.
choices.explanation: The United Nations was designed to keep the Allies cooperating after 1945, and the blocs hardened afterward rather than before the war ended.
choices.misconception: reverses the chronology of the UN and the Cold War blocs

choices.text: The Alliance was held together only by a common enemy, masking ideological differences that surfaced once Germany was defeated

items.dokRationale: The student must read a source and infer what it implies about the alliance's durability — drawing a conclusion from evidence, which is DOK-2. Naming the three Allies would be DOK-1.
items.explanation: Kennan's prescient observation captures the fundamental weakness of the wartime Allied coalition: the U.S., Britain, and the Soviet Union had vastly different political systems, ideological commitments, and postwar goals. The only thing binding them was a common enemy. Once Germany was defeated, these differences rapidly emerged, leading to the Cold War. The ideological conflict between Western liberal democracy and Soviet communism made postwar cooperation impossible. Option A is incorrect because the differences were ideological and political, not merely personal between leaders. Option B is incorrect because economic cooperation was limited and strained even during the war. Option C is incorrect because the UN was created to manage these tensions, not a cause of the breakdown.
items.explanationEs: El extracto afirma que la alianza se sostenía únicamente en un enemigo común. Esto implica que, al desaparecer ese enemigo, las diferencias ideológicas entre las democracias occidentales y la Unión Soviética quedarían al descubierto, lo que ocurrió al terminar la guerra.

items.explanation: Reagan's characterization of the Berlin Wall as a structure that 'imprisons' people rather than defends them highlights that it was built to prevent East Germans from escaping to West Berlin — not to defend against Western invasion. Option B is incorrect because the Wall was built by East Germany/the USSR, not the West. Option C is incorrect because NATO's role was about military defense, not building walls. Option D is incorrect because the Wall divided Berlin within Germany, not the German-Polish border.

choices.text: The Berlin Airlift, in which the U.S. committed massive resources to supply West Berlin rather than allowing Soviet blockade to succeed.
choices.textEs: El puente aéreo de Berlín, en el que EE.UU. comprometió enormes recursos para abastecer a Berlín Occidental en lugar de permitir que el bloqueo soviético tuviera éxito.

choices.text: The Marshall Plan's requirement that European nations adopt free-market economic policies as a condition of receiving aid.

items.explanation: The Vietnam War is the strongest validation of the critique that the Truman Doctrine's open-ended language would draw the U.S. into costly, ill-defined commitments. Policymakers used containment logic—the same framework as the Truman Doctrine—to justify escalating intervention in Vietnam, a conflict that was as much a civil war and anti-colonial struggle as it was Soviet-sponsored communism. The result was a decade of costly war with no clear victory, exactly what critics of sweeping commitments feared.
items.explanationEs: La Guerra de Vietnam es la validación más sólida de la crítica de que el lenguaje abierto de la Doctrina Truman arrastraría a EE.UU. a compromisos costosos y mal definidos. Los responsables políticos usaron la lógica de la contención para justificar la escalada de la intervención en Vietnam, un conflicto que era tanto una guerra civil y una lucha anticolonial como comunismo patrocinado por los soviéticos.

items.explanation: While the airlift succeeded in sustaining West Berlin and forced the Soviets to end the blockade, it also hardened the division of Germany and of Berlin itself, making permanent partition more likely. The immediate crisis was resolved, but the underlying problem—a divided Germany with a vulnerable, isolated West Berlin deep inside Soviet-controlled territory—remained and would generate future crises (including the 1961 Berlin Wall). Calling it an 'unqualified' victory overlooks these long-term costs.
items.explanationEs: Si bien el puente aéreo tuvo éxito al sostener a Berlín Occidental y obligar a los soviéticos a levantar el bloqueo, también endureció la división de Alemania y del propio Berlín, haciendo más probable la partición permanente. La crisis inmediata se resolvió, pero el problema subyacente —una Alemania dividida con un Berlín Occidental vulnerable y aislado dentro del territorio controlado por los soviéticos— permaneció y generaría futuras crisis.

items.stem: Across the full arc of Cold War history from 1947 to 1991, historians debate whether U.S. containment policy was primarily reactive—responding to Soviet provocations—or primarily assertive—actively shaping the international environment to American advantage. Which of the following MOST accurately represents the balance of evidence?
items.stemEs: A lo largo del arco completo de la historia de la Guerra Fría de 1947 a 1991, los historiadores debaten si la política de contención de EE.UU. fue principalmente reactiva —respondiendo a provocaciones soviéticas— o principalmente asertiva —moldeando activamente el entorno internacional en beneficio de EE.UU. ¿Cuál de las siguientes opciones representa MÁS acertadamente el balance de la evidencia?

choices.text: Containment was consistently reactive throughout the Cold War; every U.S. intervention was a direct response to a prior Soviet or Soviet-sponsored provocation, with no instances of American-initiated aggression.
choices.textEs: La contención fue consistentemente reactiva durante toda la Guerra Fría; cada intervención de EE.UU. fue una respuesta directa a una provocación soviética o patrocinada por los soviéticos previa, sin instancias de agresión iniciada por EE.UU.

choices.text: Containment blended reactive and assertive elements: some actions clearly responded to Soviet moves, while others—like CIA-sponsored coups, the Bay of Pigs, and Reagan Doctrine rollback efforts—represented American-initiated actions that exceeded a purely defensive posture.
choices.textEs: La contención mezcló elementos reactivos y asertivos: algunas acciones respondieron claramente a los movimientos soviéticos, mientras que otras —como los golpes patrocinados por la CIA, Bahía de Cochinos y los esfuerzos de reversión de la Doctrina Reagan— representaron acciones iniciadas por EE.UU. que superaron una postura puramente defensiva.

choices.text: Containment was primarily assertive throughout: U.S. policymakers consistently chose escalation over negotiation, and there is no historical evidence that the U.S. ever responded to Soviet overtures for peaceful settlement.
choices.textEs: La contención fue principalmente asertiva durante todo el período: los responsables políticos de EE.UU. eligieron consistentemente la escalada sobre la negociación, y no hay evidencia histórica de que EE.UU. respondiera a propuestas soviéticas de acuerdo pacífico.

choices.text: Containment's reactive or assertive character depended entirely on which political party held the presidency: Democrats were always reactive while Republicans were always assertive in their Cold War strategies.
choices.textEs: El carácter reactivo o asertivo de la contención dependió enteramente de qué partido político ocupaba la presidencia: los demócratas fueron siempre reactivos mientras los republicanos fueron siempre asertivos en sus estrategias de la Guerra Fría.

items.explanation: The historical record shows containment was neither purely reactive nor purely assertive—it mixed both elements depending on administration, region, and circumstance. Some actions were clearly reactive (Berlin Airlift responding to Soviet blockade, Korean War responding to North Korean invasion). Others were assertive or even aggressive (CIA coups in Iran 1953 and Guatemala 1954, Bay of Pigs, Vietnam escalation, Reagan Doctrine supporting anti-communist insurgencies). The most sophisticated historical analysis recognizes containment as a flexible, sometimes contradictory strategy that combined reactive defense with assertive rollback impulses, shaped more by domestic political pressures, specific presidential doctrines, and regional opportunism than by a consistent, coherent strategic vision.
items.explanationEs: El registro histórico muestra que la contención no fue ni puramente reactiva ni puramente asertiva —mezcló ambos elementos dependiendo de la administración, la región y las circunstancias. Algunas acciones fueron claramente reactivas (el puente aéreo de Berlín respondiendo al bloqueo soviético, la Guerra de Corea respondiendo a la invasión norcoreana). Otras fueron asertivas o incluso agresivas (golpes de la CIA en Irán 1953 y Guatemala 1954, Bahía de Cochinos, escalada de Vietnam, Doctrina Reagan apoyando insurgencias anticomunistas). El análisis histórico más sofisticado reconoce la contención como una estrategia flexible y a veces contradictoria.

items.explanation: Containment (Truman Doctrine) treated the Soviet Union as an adversary to be prevented from expanding, often through confrontational means. Option A conflates détente with appeasement. Option B incorrectly describes containment. Option C misrepresents détente's goals.
items.explanationEs: La contención (Doctrina Truman) trataba a la Unión Soviética como un adversario que debía impedirse que se expandiera, a menudo por medios confrontacionales. La distensión, desarrollada por Nixon y Kissinger, aceptó el poder soviético como una realidad permanente y buscó gestionar la relación mediante acuerdos negociados (SALT I), vínculos comerciales y reconocimiento mutuo de las esferas de influencia, reduciendo el riesgo de conflicto militar directo.

items.stem: The Truman Doctrine (1947) pledged American support for free peoples resisting subjugation, while the Marshall Plan (1947) committed roughly $13 billion to European economic reconstruction. How do these two initiatives together reflect a coherent and unified strategic logic for containing Soviet influence in postwar Europe?

choices.text: The Truman Doctrine and Marshall Plan were complementary primarily through their combined military and security dimensions — both relied on American military guarantees to deter Soviet armed aggression, with economic aid functioning as a secondary incentive to maintain Western-aligned governments.

The two initiatives reflected the strategic insight that communism thrived in conditions of economic desperation and political instability — military containment alone would be insufficient if poverty created conditions in which Soviet-backed political movements could gain genuine popular support, making economic reconstruction a strategic necessity rather than purely humanitarian charity.

Truman and Marshall designed their respective programs as deliberate provocations intended to force the Soviet Union into an unsustainable military competition, representing early applications of the rollback strategy later associated with Eisenhower's New Look defense policy.

The Truman Doctrine established a global ideological framework for containment, but the Marshall Plan was primarily motivated by American economic self-interest in creating prosperous European export markets — suggesting that strategic and commercial interests happened to align in this case rather than reflecting a single coherent anti-Soviet vision.

items.explanation: The Truman Doctrine and Marshall Plan embodied the strategic insight that communism was not primarily a military threat in postwar Western Europe but a political one — vulnerable populations under economic stress might turn to communist parties offering material solutions, making economic stabilization a direct instrument of political containment.

items.stem: The Korean War (1950-53) ended in an armistice that restored the pre-war division of Korea approximately at the 38th parallel — the same boundary that had existed before the North Korean invasion. How does the Korean War outcome most accurately illustrate the operational constraints that containment doctrine imposed on American military strategy?

choices.text: The Korean War demonstrated that the United States could successfully defend Cold War commitments through limited military engagement without triggering direct conflict with China or the Soviet Union, fully validating containment doctrine's assumption that graduated military force could deter communist expansion at acceptable cost.

The Korean stalemate showed that containment was strategically inadequate because it merely restored the prewar status quo rather than liberating communist-controlled territory, confirming that only a more aggressive rollback policy could effectively reduce the Soviet sphere.

Korea demonstrated that the United Nations could function as an effective collective security mechanism when major powers reached consensus on responding to aggression, suggesting multilateral frameworks rather than unilateral American containment were the most viable approach to communist expansion.

Korea illustrated that containment doctrine created a fundamental tension between achieving complete military victory and avoiding escalation into general war with nuclear powers — Truman's dismissal of MacArthur reflected the judgment that containment's objectives were inherently limited and that expanding the war against China would not serve American strategic interests even if it produced tactical

items.explanation: Truman's firing of MacArthur is the clearest illustration of containment's operational logic: MacArthur's proposal to expand the war risked general conflict with China and possible Soviet intervention, which Truman judged would transform a limited defensive action into the global conflict that containment was specifically designed to prevent even at the cost of local military advantages.

items.stem:
Read the following excerpt from President Harry S. Truman's Address to Congress, March 12, 1947 — a U.S. government document available through the Avalon Project, Yale Law School, and the National Archives:

"I believe that it must be the policy of the United States to support free peoples who are resisting attempted subjugation by armed minorities or by outside pressures. I believe that we must assist free peoples to work out their own destinies in their own way. I believe that our help should be primarily through economic and financial aid which is essential to economic stability and orderly political processes."

Using this excerpt and your knowledge of U.S. Cold War foreign policy (US.60–US.62), write a CER response that evaluates the Truman Doctrine as both a foreign policy commitment and an ideological statement. Your response must analyze how the Doctrine set the precedent for later Cold War interventions and assess whether Truman's framing was primarily a reaction to immediate crises in Greece and Turkey or a broader ideological declaration with long-term global consequences.
items.stemEs:
Lee el siguiente fragmento del Discurso del Presidente Harry S. Truman ante el Congreso, 12 de marzo de 1947 — un documento del gobierno de EE. UU. disponible a través del Proyecto Avalon de la Escuela de Derecho de Yale y los Archivos Nacionales:

"Creo que debe ser la política de los Estados Unidos apoyar a los pueblos libres que resisten la subyugación intentada por minorías armadas o por presiones externas. Creo que debemos ayudar a los pueblos libres a trabajar en sus propios destinos a su propia manera. Creo que nuestra ayuda debe ser principalmente a través de ayuda económica y financiera que es esencial para la estabilidad económica y los procesos políticos ordenados."

Usando este fragmento y tu conocimiento de la política exterior de EE. UU. durante la Guerra Fría (US.60–US.62), escribe una respuesta CER que evalúe la Doctrina Truman tanto como compromiso de política exterior como como declaración ideológica. Tu respuesta debe analizar cómo la Doctrina estableció el precedente para intervenciones posteriores de la Guerra Fría.
items.correctAnswer: A top-scoring (4/4) response would include: CLAIM — The Truman Doctrine was simultaneously a response to immediate crises and a sweeping ideological declaration that transformed U.S. foreign policy from selective engagement to open-ended global commitment against communist expansion, establishing a precedent that justified Cold War interventions for decades. EVIDENCE — (1) The immediate context: civil war in Greece (communist guerrillas vs. monarchy) and Soviet pressure on Turkey for access to the Dardanelles Strait — both situations Britain could no longer afford to manage after WWII; (2) Truman's language is explicitly universal ('free peoples... in their own way') rather than geographically limited, signaling a doctrine rather than a one-time aid package; (3) the $400 million aid package to Greece and Turkey as the practical expression; (4) the Marshall Plan (1948, US.61) as the economic counterpart; (5) the Korean War (US.63) and later Vietnam as direct precedential applications of the Doctrine's logic. REASONING — The student should reason that Truman's framing as an ideological statement — rather than simply an emergency aid bill — was a deliberate choice to build congressional and public support by casting the conflict in Manichean terms (free vs. enslaved peoples). This framing had long-term consequences: it committed the U.S. to supporting any anti-communist government regardless of its democratic credentials, a tension visible in later Cold War alliances with authoritarian regimes.
items.dokRationale: Student must synthesize across multiple standards and sources, constructing an extended argument that connects US.60, US.62 through evidence-based reasoning requiring sustained analytical writing.
items.explanation:
SCORING GUIDE (4 points):
4 - Exemplary: Precise claim addresses both dimensions of the prompt (immediate crisis AND ideological declaration). Evidence includes at least three specific historical details: immediate Greece/Turkey context, universal language of the speech, at least one later precedential application (Korea, Vietnam, etc.). Reasoning addresses the tension between anti-communism and democratic values embedded in the Doctrine. CER fully developed and integrated.
3 - Proficient: Clear claim. Two specific pieces of evidence. Reasoning makes the precedent connection but may not develop the ideological tension or long-term consequences fully.
2 - Developing: General claim about U.S. containment. One piece of specific evidence. Reasoning describes rather than analyzes (e.g., 'the U.S. helped Greece and Turkey').
1 - Beginning: Vague or inaccurate claim. Minimal evidence. No real reasoning.
0 - No response or off-topic.

KEY EVIDENCE EXPECTED: Greek Civil War (1946–1949); Soviet pressure on Turkey (Dardanelles); British withdrawal from the region; $400 million aid appropriation; Marshall Plan as economic companion; Korean War (1950) as first major precedential application; 'police action' justification in Korea; later Vietnam War application; NSC-68 escalation.
items.explanationEs:
GUÍA DE PUNTUACIÓN (4 puntos):
4 - Ejemplar: La afirmación precisa aborda ambas dimensiones del indicador (crisis inmediata Y declaración ideológica). La evidencia incluye al menos tres detalles históricos específicos. El razonamiento aborda la tensión entre el anticomunismo y los valores democráticos. CER completamente desarrollado.
3 - Competente: Afirmación clara. Dos piezas de evidencia específica. El razonamiento hace la conexión de precedente pero puede no desarrollar la tensión ideológica.
2 - En desarrollo: Afirmación general sobre la contención de EE. UU. Una pieza de evidencia específica. El razonamiento describe en lugar de analizar.
1 - Inicial: Afirmación vaga o inexacta. Evidencia mínima. Sin razonamiento real.
0 - Sin respuesta o fuera del tema.

EVIDENCIA CLAVE ESPERADA: Guerra Civil Griega (1946–1949); presión soviética sobre Turquía; retirada británica de la región; apropiación de $400 millones en ayuda; Plan Marshall como acompañante económico; Guerra de Corea (1950) como primera aplicación de precedente; aplicación posterior de la Guerra de Vietnam.

"The issues that face us are momentous, involving the fulfillment or destruction not only of this Republic but of civilization itself. They are issues which will not await our deliberation... Una derrota de las instituciones libres en cualquier lugar es una derrota en todas partes."

Directions: Read the following three primary source excerpts and then respond to the prompt below. In your response, analyze each document using the HIPP framework (Historical context, Intended audience, Purpose, Point of view) and construct an evidence-based argument.

---
DOCUMENT A: George Kennan, "The Long Telegram," February 22, 1946 — declassified U.S. State Department cable, available through the National Archives:
"We have here a political force committed fanatically to the belief that with US there can be no permanent modus vivendi, that it is desirable and necessary that the internal harmony of our society be disrupted, our traditional way of life be destroyed, the international authority of our state be broken, if Soviet power is to be secured."

DOCUMENT B: Winston Churchill, "The Sinews of Peace" (Iron Curtain Speech), Westminster College, Fulton, Missouri, March 5, 1946 — public address, transcript available through Westminster College archives:
"From Stettin in the Baltic to Trieste in the Adriatic, an iron curtain has descended across the Continent. Behind that line lie all the capitals of the ancient states of Central and Eastern Europe... all are subject in one form or another, not only to Soviet influence but to a very high and in many cases increasing measure of control from Moscow."

DOCUMENT C: Harry S. Truman, Address to Congress (Truman Doctrine), March 12, 1947 — U.S. government document, National Archives:
"At the present moment in world history nearly every nation must choose between alternative ways of life. The choice is too often not a free one. One way of life is based upon the will of the majority... The second way of life is based upon the will of a minority forcibly imposed upon the majority."

---
Using all three documents and your knowledge of Cold War origins (US.59–US.60), construct an argument that evaluates the relative roles of ideology and geopolitical strategy in causing the Cold War. Apply HIPP analysis to at least two of the three documents and use outside historical knowledge to support your argument. Your response should address: (1) what each document reveals about U.S./Western perceptions of the Soviet threat; (2) whether the Cold War was primarily an ideological conflict or a geopolitical competition for power; and (3) whether alternative outcomes were possible given the structural conditions of 1945–1947.

HIPP ANALYSIS (minimum 2 documents): Document A — Historical context: Kennan writes from Moscow in 1946, observing Soviet consolidation of Eastern Europe; Intended audience: U.S. State Department and policymakers; Purpose: To convince Washington that Soviet behavior requires a long-term strategic response; Point of view: Kennan projects ideological determination onto the Soviets, though his later writings suggest he overestimated the ideological element and underestimated pragmatic Soviet nationalism. Document B — Historical context: Churchill speaks as a private citizen (no longer PM) on American soil, 9 months after WWII ended; Intended audience: American public and policymakers (Truman was present); Purpose: To galvanize Western resolve against Soviet expansion; Point of view: Churchill's 'iron curtain' framing is geopolitical but presented in ideological terms — he sees Soviet expansion as inherently threatening regardless of its ideological character. Document C — Historical context: 14 months after Kennan's telegram; Intended audience: Congress and the American people; Purpose: To secure funding for Greece and Turkey; Point of view: Truman frames the conflict in ideological binary terms ('will of majority vs. minority forcibly imposed') that goes beyond Greece and Turkey to make a universal claim. OUTSIDE EVIDENCE: Soviet behavior at Yalta and Potsdam; Soviet rejection of Marshall Plan (1947); Berlin Blockade (1948); Soviet atomic bomb test (1949); Communist victory in China (1949). ALTERNATIVE OUTCOMES: The student should address whether Soviet-American cooperation was possible given the structural asymmetries — security dilemma, competing reconstruction interests in Germany, and ideological distrust that pre-dated 1945. SYNTHESIS: The three documents show escalating American commitment to an ideological framing of what began as geopolitical competition, suggesting that U.S. policy choices helped solidify the binary that made Cold War confrontation self-reinforcing.

Directions: Read the following three primary source excerpts and respond to the prompt below. Apply HIPP analysis to at least two documents and construct an argument.

---
DOCUMENT A: President Harry S. Truman, Statement on the Berlin Airlift, July 19, 1948 — U.S. government document, available through the Harry S. Truman Presidential Library (National Archives):
"We are in Berlin as a result of our agreements with our Allies after the defeat of Germany... These agreements also gave us certain rights of access to Berlin. I want the record to be absolutely clear that abandonment of our position in Berlin would mean the loss of more than a city. It would be a blow to the entire structure of resistance to Soviet expansionism."

DOCUMENT B: North Atlantic Treaty, Preamble and Article 5, April 4, 1949 — multilateral treaty, available through the Avalon Project, Yale Law School:
"The Parties... are determined to safeguard the freedom, common heritage and civilisation of their peoples, founded on the principles of democracy, individual liberty and the rule of law... The Parties agree that an armed attack against one or more of them in Europe or North America shall be considered an attack against them all."

DOCUMENT C: President John F. Kennedy, "Ich bin ein Berliner" speech, West Berlin, June 26, 1963 — U.S. government document, available through the John F. Kennedy Presidential Library (National Archives):
"There are many people in the world who really don't understand, or say they don't, what is the great issue between the free world and the Communist world. Let them come to Berlin. Freedom is indivisible, and when one man is enslaved, all are free. The wall is the most obvious and vivid demonstration of the failures of the Communist system."

---
